items.title: AI Workforce Accountability Framework
items.abstract: The AI Workforce Accountability Framework (AWAF) is a governance and risk-based model designed to bring structure, transparency, and responsibility to AI-driven workforce decisions. As organizations increasingly adopt artificial intelligence to optimize operations, workforce-related decisions are often made without adequate evaluation of human impact, long-term sustainability, or accountability. AWAF addresses this gap by introducing a structured approach that integrates governance principles into AI adoption. The framework is built on three core pillars:Human Impact Assessment, which evaluates the implications of AI-driven decisions on employees and roles;Reskilling and Transition Responsibility, which emphasizes the need for organizations to provide pathways for workforce adaptation rather than abrupt displacement; andAccountability and Transparency, which ensures that decisions are explainable, auditable, and aligned with governance standards. AWAF is designed to be applicable across industries and can serve as a foundational model for organizations seeking to implement responsible and sustainable AI strategies. The framework bridges the gap between technological innovation and human-centric governance, ensuring that AI adoption is not only efficient but also ethical and accountable.

items.title: AI-Augmented HRM Practices as Mediators of Sustainable Performance in the IT Industry: The Role of Digital Culture, Organizational Strategy, and Digital Leadership
items.abstract: The increased pace of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has reinvented human resource management (HRM) and made a difference in the approach organizations to gain, grow and sustain talents. This research study explores the relationship between Digital Culture (DC), Organizational Strategy (OS), and Digital Leadership (DL) on Sustainable Organizational Performance (SOP), with AI-Augmented HRM (AIHRM) as a moderating variable. Following a quantitative research approach, data were collected from employees of selected IT companies in Nepal using a questionnaire with predefined items. Furthermore, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed to evaluate both measurement and structural models for reliability, validity, and model fit. The findings reveal that DC, OS, and DL have significant and positive effect on AIHRM, collectively explaining 62.8% variance (R² = 0.628). Similarly, these predictors, along with AIHRM, account for 56.3% variance in SOP (R² = 0.563). Among all the predictors, OS has the strongest effect on SOP (β = 0.332, p < 0.001), which is followed by DC (β = 0.314, p < 0.001) and DL (β = 0.234, p < 0.001). AIHRM positively, though small, directly influences SOP (β = 0.122, p < 0.001) and is a good partial mediator between organizational variables and sustainability performances.

items.title: AI-Driven Personalised Learning and Girls’ Educational Outcomes in Nigeria: Implications for Achieving SDGs 4 and 5
items.abstract: Despite its large population and economy, Nigeria faces persistent gender disparities in accessing and completing quality education, especially for girls in rural and northern regions, where early marriage, poverty‑related domestic responsibilities, and infrastructural deficits intersect to impede progress on girls’ schooling. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven personalised learning platforms and AI‑enhanced teacher‑support tools are emerging as central components of the country’s Education Reform Agenda, promising to improve access, quality, and equity through adaptive content, individualised feedback, and real‑time diagnostics. Drawing on secondary data from national reports on SDG 4 and SDG 5, education‑statistics databases, and a range of Artificial Intelligence in Education (AI‑in‑Ed) case studies, this article critically investigates how AI‑driven personalised learning is associated with girls’ learning outcomes, retention, and dropout rates in Nigeria. The analysis focuses on secondary‑level education and uses national and sub‑national indicators from UNESCO, UNICEF, the World Bank, and Nigerian government agencies to compare educational settings with and without AI‑innovation pilots or AI‑teacher‑support systems. Findings indicate that when girls use AI-driven personalised tools within structured, teacher-facilitated environments, their learning gains subject-specific performance and progression rates improve relative to their non-AI-exposed peers. The study also highlights significant risks of deepening the gender‑digital divide if AI‑deployment is uneven across regions, schools, and socio‑economic strata or if algorithms incorporate and reproduce gender‑based biases in assessment, tracking, and career‑guidance recommendations. This research concludes with concrete policy recommendations for integrating gender‑sensitive Artificial Intelligence (AI) design, gender‑disaggregated monitoring, and targeted infrastructure investments into national AI‑in‑education strategies, to advance SDG 4 (inclusive and equitable quality education) and SDG 5 (gender equality and women’s empowerment) in a more equitable and transformative manner.

items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in language education has significantly transformed traditional teaching approaches, particularly through the use of authentic video materials. Authentic videos, which reflect real-life language use, provide learners with meaningful context and exposure to natural communication. When combined with AI technologies, these materials become more interactive, adaptive, and effective in developing higher-order thinking skills and communicative competence. This study explores how AI-enhanced authentic video materials contribute to the development of students’ critical thinking and communicative skills in foreign language learning. AI tools such as speech recognition systems, automated feedback platforms, and intelligent tutoring systems enable personalized learning experiences and real-time evaluation. The research also examines the pedagogical benefits and challenges of integrating AI into video-based instruction. The findings suggest that AI-supported authentic video materials significantly improve learners’ engagement, analytical abilities, and communication skills. However, effective implementation requires a balanced approach that combines technological innovation with pedagogical guidance.

items.title: Algorithmic Agency and the Posthuman Economy: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of Economic Decision-Making
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is fundamentally reshaping contemporary economic systems as algorithmic infrastructures increasingly participate in interpreting information, generating predictions, and influencing organizational decision-making. While much of the business and management literature approaches artificial intelligence primarily as a technological capability that enhances efficiency and productivity, emerging posthumanist scholarship suggests a deeper transformation in which economic agency itself becomes distributed across human and algorithmic actors. This article develops the concept of algorithmic agency to explain how artificial intelligence participates in economic decision-making within modern business systems. Drawing on posthumanist theory, socio-technical research, and digital economy scholarship, the study argues that contemporary organizations operate within hybrid intelligence environments where human expertise and algorithmic systems collaboratively produce economic knowledge, prediction, and action. By conceptualizing the emergence of a posthuman economy, this study contributes to interdisciplinary debates on artificial intelligence, digital capitalism, and the transformation of economic organization.

items.title: An Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Application from the Perspective of Marx’s View of Machinery
items.abstract: Marx’s view of machinery provides a scientific theoretical foundation for understanding the application of artificial intelligence (AI). AI represents the intellectualization of machinery construction and is, in essence, a further extension of human organs. Under capitalist application, AI is reduced to an instrument of capital exploitation, giving rise to problems such as the displacement of workers, labor intensification, field penetration, and labor alienation. Based on a critique of the capitalist application of AI, the reverse construction of a socialist application scheme for AI is of great significance for enabling people to achieve smooth employment and labor, reduce the burden of work, share development dividends, and move steadily toward free and all‑round development in the era of AI.

items.title: An Analysis of Factors Influencing AI Adoption among Higher Education Students
items.abstract: As the digital transformation of global higher education deepens, the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools is profoundly reshaping educational paradigms and academic collaboration models. However, most current research focuses solely on single technical attributes such as accuracy or processing speed, with a significant lack of exploration into the interplay between institutional policies, cultural orientations, and individual socioeconomic status. This study employs the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) as its core analytical framework—effectively explaining individual adoption—to investigate the combined effects of technological attributes, institutional environments, and individual differences on university students' willingness and depth of AI tool adoption. It examines three primary cases: the campus proliferation of Grammarly, the Russell Group's ethical policy formation process, and ChatGPT's progressive payment model. Findings reveal that perceived value is a necessary condition for technology adoption, while meso-level institutional orientations and normative ethical reasoning serve as key variables moderating students' technological readiness and reducing adoption anxiety. Notably, income disparities are emerging as an invisible technological barrier.

items.title: Analysing the mediating relationship between using artificial intelligence and threats to professional identity
items.abstract: The article analyses employees’ assessments related to the consequences of using artificial intelligence (AI) in their workplaces. The paper highlights subjective risks that threaten the professional identity of employees, namely: changes in job functions, devaluation of human capital, and job loss. The formation of these risks relates to the experience of using AI in the workplace. The study tests two hypotheses regarding the formation of threats to an employee’s professional identity: the first one is that the threat of losing professional identity is more characteristic for employees who have no experience of using AI (the fear hypothesis); the second one links the threat of losing professional identity with experience in using AI (the awareness hypothesis). Based on empirical data from the 33rd wave of the RLMS-HSE, we analyse a model in which experience of interacting with AI in the workplace acts as a mediating factor determining this fear. The results of Bayesian mediation analysis confirm the awareness hypothesis. The use of AI in the workplace increases the threat to professional identity. Based on the results obtained, we conclude that it is feasible to revise strategies for adapting to digitalisation and that it is important to shift the focus to developing skills in employees that cannot be automated. In the business environment, communications focused on replacing labour with AI should be reoriented towards increasing employee productivity with the help of AI.

items.title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE ANALYSIS OF COMPANY BUSINESS PROCESSES
items.abstract: This article explores how artificial intelligence can be used for business process analysis and predictive modeling in the context of digital entrepreneurship. The growth in the volume of operational data, combined with the need for greater forecasting accuracy in an increasingly unstable business environment, underscores the relevance of this research. In recent years, companies have been actively integrating artificial intelligence tools into their process analytics, thereby strengthening the evidence base for informed management decisions and reducing operating costs. The purpose of the study is to provide a theoretical justification and analysis of the practical aspects of applying artificial intelligence in the analysis of companies' business processes, as well as to identify key areas and prerequisites for the implementation of AI technologies to improve the effectiveness of management decision-making in the context of digital entrepreneurship. A comparative analysis of conventional statistical methods and machine learning approaches was conducted, evaluating each against criteria such as data handling capacity, forecasting accuracy, model development speed, and responsiveness to changing conditions. The respective strengths and limitations of both approaches were systematized with a focus on their practical applicability in trading enterprises. The study is based on analytical reports from international companies. It has been established that the most sought-after areas are the detection of anomalies in data, analytics for improving forecasts, and operational support for decisions. The feasibility of using combined approaches, in particular neural networks for short-term and autoregressive models for long-term forecasts, has been substantiated. The key factors for successful implementation of systems have been identified, including data quality, the level of digital literacy of personnel, and ensuring the interpretability of results. The practical significance of the work lies in the development of recommended guidelines for selecting the optimal artificial intelligence tools for various business process analytics tasks, depending on the specifics of the enterprise's activities and strategic business objectives.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence Technology in Optimizing Homestay Space Design
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence technology is evolving rapidly, and its application in various fields is becoming more and more extensive, and the bunkhouse industry is no exception. In order to make bunkhouses more competitive and appealing, this study explores the possibilities of artificial intelligence technologies to optimize space arrangement and improve user experience. Research methods include literature research, user interviews and expert consultation. This study has built an evaluation system containing 5 dimensions and 18 factor indicators, and on this basis, the bunkhouse space design scheme generated by artificial intelligence is studied. The study used importance analysis (IPA) to analyze the importance and satisfaction of each factor indicator. The findings demonstrate that consumers are aware of and pleased with the artificial intelligence-generated bunkhouse space design scheme’s information communication and creative beauty dimensions. The study comes to the conclusion that increasing user happiness with AI-driven bunkhouse design requires enhancing its usability and experience quality.

items.title: Architectural Design in the Age of Generative AI: Toward a Balance Between Efficiency and Responsibility
items.abstract: Since 2022-23, the rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has begun to reshape architectural design practice. Beyond accelerating design efficiency, generative AI is redefining creativity, professional expertise, and the ethical responsibilities of architects. This study examines both optimistic and skeptical perspectives on generative AI in architecture through a critical narrative review drawing on practitioner publications, professional discourse, and academic literature. The optimistic view highlights productivity, creative expansion, and data-driven sustainability, whereas the skeptical view raises concerns about professional deskilling, cultural bias, black-box opacity, and environmental costs. Synthesizing these tensions, the paper proposes an integrated framework built on three practical agendas: (1) redefining the architect’s role from passive approver to critical curator who strategically evaluates and integrates AI-generated outcomes; (2) establishing ethical governance to ensure transparency, fairness, and sustainability in AI-assisted design; and (3) reforming architectural education to cultivate integrative practitioners capable of critical reasoning and interdisciplinary collaboration. This study provides a roadmap for integrating generative AI into architectural practice in ways that enhance both efficiency and social responsibility.

items.abstract: This paper critically examines the implications of artificial intelligence for literary creativity, authorship, and the philosophy of language. As large language models demonstrate increasingly sophisticated capacities for generating coherent, stylistically varied, and contextually appropriate prose and poetry, fundamental assumptions about the nature of literary creativity, originality, and meaning are called into question. The study draws upon philosophical aesthetics, computational linguistics, and contemporary literary theory to investigate three central questions: whether AI-generated texts can be considered literature, how AI challenges Romantic and modernist conceptions of authorship, and what the rise of AI writing means for the future of human literary expression. The paper argues for a collaborative model of human-AI literary production that neither romanticizes human creativity nor reduces it to computation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of the Mathematical Paradigm: From Computation to Theorem Discovery
items.abstract: This study examines the transformative role of artificial intelligence in the field of mathematics. With the rapid advancement of machine learning and neural networks, artificial intelligence has evolved from a merely computational tool into an intelligent collaborator in mathematical discovery. By reviewing key areas such as symbolic computation, automated theorem proving, optimization, and the analysis of complex patterns in number theory, this article shows how the integration of human reasoning with the processing speed of machines has opened new horizons for solving previously unresolved problems. Finally, by examining the epistemological and ethical challenges involved in using algorithms in mathematical proofs, the future of mathematics is explained as a collaborative field between human beings and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Implementation in Human Resources Management: Opportunities, Challenges, and Strategic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract - Artificial Intelligence (AI) is significantly changing Human Resources (HR) management, especially in multinational companies. In recent times, we have seen most of the HR functions such as talent acquisition, employee onboarding, performance monitoring, and many more have started adopting AI based solutions. In this paper, the impact of AI across these core HR activities by reviewing research papers, industry reports, and case studies published between 2018 and 2026 is investigated. In this study, we can see how AI can improve the efficiency and effectiveness of data-driven decision making. Also, there are some challenges like algorithmic bias, data privacy, regulatory concerns, and human-technology interaction. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Strategic AI Integration Framework (SAIF), which provides a structured approach for organizations so that they can adopt AI in HR in a responsible manner. Our analysis of current HR trends shows that AI integration delivers more than just theoretical value. It has shortened recruitment cycles by 40% and pushed retention rates up by nearly 25%. These gains in L&D and hiring are significant, but they are not guaranteed. Success depends on a human centred approach with a solid plan for organizational change, rather than just deploying the software. Professionals believe that AI will be a standard feature in HR workflows within five years. However, in spite of all the enthusiasm, organizations are struggling with questions of implementation strategies, ethical governance, adoption by employees, and the most important factor, return on investment. This paper addresses these gaps by: 1. providing a detailed review of applications of AI across the HR value chain, 2. critically reviewing the challenges associated with it, such as bias, privacy, and change management, 3. presenting measurable evidence of the impact of AI, and 4. proposing a Strategic AI Integration Framework (SAIF) to guide HR leaders responsible for the adoption of AI. This paper is organized into eight sections. Section II presents a review of the relevant literature, followed by the research methodology in Section III. Section IV explores the applications of artificial intelligence in human resources, while Section V examines the associated challenges. Section VI introduces the Strategic AI Integration Framework (SAIF), Section VII discusses the key findings, and Section VIII concludes with recommendations.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in breast cancer: applications and advancements
items.abstract: Breast cancer is the most common malignant tumor among women globally and poses a major public health challenge due to limitations in traditional diagnostic and treatment processes, such as subjective interpretation biases and inefficient multi-dimensional data integration. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning and machine learning technologies, has emerged as a transformative tool in addressing these issues. Clinically, AI has been widely applied in imaging screening to improve detection rates and reduce reading time, digital pathology for precise tumor typing and gene mutation prediction, treatment decision-support systems to enhance guideline compliance, and drug research and development to accelerate target identification and virtual screening. Despite these achievements, AI implementation faces challenges, such as data standardization issues, limited model generalization, low clinical accessibility, and unclear ethical-legal responsibilities, which require targeted solutions that include national data standards, multi-center training, hierarchical physician training, and explainable AI. Future directions involve multi-modal data integration, human-AI collaborative multidisciplinary team models, and extension to full-cycle health management from prevention-to-rehabilitation. This review provides a systematic overview of the role of AI in breast cancer care, offering insights for clinical practice and scientific research innovation, and supporting the transition toward personalized and intelligent medicine in oncology.
